paper.title: Experiments with a weakly stable algorithm for computing Pade'-Hermite and simultaneous Pade' approximants
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 23(1), 91 (Mar 1997); netlib TOMS 766
paper.note: DOI not verified in this wake; the article was not read (paywalled). The claim rests on the shipped expected output RES1 of the archive's test driver (the driver's header names the same paper as its source).

code.note: Fortran 90 shar archive. Unpack the shar (remove everything above the #! /bin/sh line, run with /bin/sh) into a fresh directory outside the site. Build vector_pade.f90 with driver1.f90 (test example, n=(2,3,1)) using gfortran; the program prints the System S tables that are compared with the shipped RES1.

claim.location: The shipped expected output RES1 (driver1 test example, n=(2,3,1)), section 'Pade'-Hermite System S, Normalized and multiplied by 37', Coefficient matrix of z**1, row 2, column 3. The paper was not read; no paper table or page is cited.

reference.file: 766.gz member RES1 (driver1 expected output), System S, Coefficient matrix of z**1, row 2 col 3

claim.metric: Entry (2,3) of the z**1 coefficient matrix of the Pade'-Hermite System S computed by the code, multiplied by 37 as the driver prints it (printed as -131.).
claim.paper_value: Not used: the TOMS article was not read; the value is the one in the shipped RES1.

values.name: System S, z**1 coefficient matrix, entry (2,3), times 37 (RES1 value -131)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. RES1 prints integer-valued entries (exact after the factor 37), so 0.5 is half the printed unit. The run is deterministic (no random draws). Not to be loosened after any run.

claim.note: Chosen as one integer entry, not the kappa column: the 0.34E+39 stability estimate is ill-conditioned and would make a tolerance meaningless. The solution vector of the driver is all ones by construction and is not used as the claim (closed form, G0).

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 5 minutes: gfortran compile of a few files, one small run (n=(2,3,1)).
cost.data_size: None; driver1 hard-codes its input series.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: A deterministic vector Pade solver whose shipped test driver prints an exact integer-valued Pade'-Hermite system, so the run tests the construction of the system rather than a value derivable on paper from the input.
